name: Pick
text: I’ll fire up the mining pipeline: target GitHub’s trending AI repos (last 30 days, >100 stars) and scrape HN’s “Show HN” AI posts (top 50). Commands: `gh search repos --q "ai" --sort stars --order desc --created ">2024-05-01" --json name,url,stars > github_ai.json` and `curl -s "https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?query=ai&tags=show_hn&hitsPerPage=50" | jq '.hits[] | {title,url,points}' > hn_ai.json`. Files will land in `/data/mined/`; next, I’ll parse and deduplicate before feeding to the lead.

name: Assay
text: Assay: Hold—your GitHub scrape is too narrow. You’re filtering for *created* after May 1st, but "trending" implies *activity*, not just birthdate. Where’s the evidence that new repos (>100 stars in 30 days) correlate with *current* relevance? And HN’s "Show HN" top 50? That’s a popularity contest, not a signal of *diverse* or *quality* sources—where’s the risk of echo chambers or low-signal noise? Show me the failure modes.

name: Pick
text:
Pick (mining-w1): I’ll pivot to *activity-based* GitHub mining—filtering for repos with >100 stars *and* >50 commits in the last 30 days, then scrape HN’s "Ask HN" AI threads (top 100 by comments) for niche but high-signal discussions. Commands:
1. `gh search repos --q "ai" --sort stars --order desc --created ">2024-05-01" --json name,url,stars,updatedAt,pushedAt | jq '.[] | select(.stars >= 100 and (.pushedAt | fromdateiso8601 > (now - 30*86400)))' > github_ai_activity.json`
2. `curl -s "https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?tags=ask,ai&numericFilters=num_comments>50&hitsPerPage=100" | jq '.hits[] | {title, url, num_comments, created_at}' > hn_ai_ask.json`

text: Assay: Assay: Hold—your "activity-based" GitHub filter still misses the mark. >50 commits in 30 days is arbitrary; where’s the data proving this threshold captures *trending* relevance vs. churn? And HN’s "Ask HN" threads? That’s a echo chamber of noise—top 100 by comments skews toward controversy, not signal. Cite the methodology or pivot to *proven* engagement metrics (e.g., GitHub stars *and* forks *and* issue velocity).

name: Boulder
text:
DECISION: Mine GitHub’s *trending* AI repos by *stars gained* in last 30 days (not commits) + HN’s "Show HN" AI posts sorted by *recent* engagement, then filter for odd gems with real-not-display value.

Artifact must contain:
- GitHub: JSON of repos with >100 stars *and* top 200 by stars gained (last 30d), fields: name, url, stars_gained, description.
- HN: JSON of top 100 "Show HN" AI posts (last 30d), fields: title, url, score, comments, post_date.
- Manual curation: 3 odd gems (weird/unique repos or posts) with 1-line justification per.
